overview: Teleperformance (TP) is the world's largest outsourced customer experience (CX) and business process outsourcing (BPO) provider, operating in nearly 100 countries with close to 490,000 employees and serving roughly 1,500 clients, including two-thirds of the world's 100 largest brands. The company delivers front-office customer care, technical support, sales and back-office services (Core Services, ~85% of revenue) alongside higher-margin Specialized Services such as interpreting (LanguageLine Solutions), visa/consular processing (TLScontact), accounts receivable management (AllianceOne) and recruitment process outsourcing (PSG Global Solutions). Founded in Paris in 1978 and listed on Euronext Paris, TP generated over EUR 10.2 billion of revenue in FY2025 and is now executing a CEO-led 'Future Forward' turnaround to reposition itself as an AI-augmented digital business services company after a severe, multi-year de-rating driven by fears that generative AI will disintermediate traditional contact-center labor.

business_model.summary: TP earns revenue primarily from long-term, multi-year outsourcing contracts under which it operates customer service, technical support, sales, trust & safety, and back-office functions on behalf of corporate and government clients, typically billing per FTE/seat, per transaction, or per minute, with a growing share of outcome-based and AI-powered pricing. Revenue is largely contractual/recurring (average top-100 client relationship of ~14 years) but has volume/transaction variability tied to client call/contact volumes, making it quasi-cyclical with client end-markets. Margins are a function of labor cost arbitrage (offshore/nearshore delivery), automation-driven productivity, and scale.

business_model.customer_type: B2B and B2G (government); enterprise multinationals and public-sector agencies; highly diversified client base - no single client >6% of revenue, top 10 clients ~31%, top 100 ~66%
business_model.geographic_mix: Revenue by region (Core Services, FY2025): Americas ~39%, Europe/MEA/Asia-Pacific ~46%, Specialized Services ~15% (mostly US-based). Delivery footprint spans onshore, nearshore (Mexico, Eastern Europe) and offshore (Philippines, India, Egypt) locations; ~100 countries of operation.

competitive_position.market_position: #1 global player in outsourced CX/BPO by revenue (ahead of #2 Concentrix); the core outsourced CX market (~USD 117-118bn in 2025E) is itself a subset of a far larger USD ~514bn global BPO/digital business services market where TP is pushing to expand share. TLScontact holds ~11% share of the outsourced visa-application market (VFS Global leads with ~55%).

moat_factors.description: Operations in ~100 countries with onshore/nearshore/offshore 'smartshoring' flexibility let TP serve large multinational RFPs that smaller regional players cannot match, and provide geographic diversification against single-country disruption.

Average 14-year relationship with top-100 clients; outsourced operations are deeply embedded in client workflows, data systems and compliance processes, making migration costly and risky, though RFP-driven re-tendering does occur.

moat_factors.factor: Proprietary AI/technology stack (TP.ai FAB, TP Infinity)
moat_factors.description: TP is building a proprietary AI orchestration layer and partnering with AI vendors (Microsoft, ServiceNow, Kore.ai, Sanas, Parloa, Ema) to defend its position as an AI integrator rather than pure labor arbitrage provider; durability versus in-house client AI adoption or hyperscaler-native tools is unproven.
No client over 6% of revenue and broad vertical exposure (financial services, tech, telecom, travel, healthcare, retail) reduces concentration risk relative to smaller peers.
ISO 27001, ISO 42001 (AI management), Great Place to Work certification in 69 countries support trust with large enterprise/government clients handling sensitive data.

weaknesses: Business is fundamentally people-intensive and labor-cost-arbitrage-based, structurally exposed to generative AI/agentic AI substitution of human agents
Low differentiation versus Tier 2/3 competitors on price for commoditized voice/chat work, creating ongoing margin pressure
Trust & Safety / content moderation line in structural, accelerating decline (automation plus reputational overhang)
History of execution/communication missteps with investors (2024 guidance miss, perceived slow response to AI narrative) that damaged credibility and the valuation multiple
Heavy debt load taken on for the Majorel acquisition, constraining capital flexibility during a cyclical downturn

growth_drivers: Future Forward strategic plan (launched June 2025, led by new CEO Jorge Amar from March 2026) targeting a return to mid-single-digit (4-6%) like-for-like revenue growth by 2028 and margin expansion to ~15.5% EBITA post-AI transformation

Scaling of TP.ai FAB AI orchestration suites (500+ AI projects launched in 2025) and AI-powered/back-office/outcome-based service lines, which posted double-digit growth in H1 2026 even as overall revenue declined
Continued offshoring/nearshoring migration (India, Egypt, Philippines) lowering delivery cost and partially offsetting pricing pressure
Data Services for AI (data annotation, model training support) - a new, fast-growing business line leveraging TP's global, low-cost workforce for the broader AI value chain

M&A-driven diversification into high value-added Specialized Services (Majorel 2023, ZP Better Together 2025, Agents Only 2025) and the newly launched portfolio strategic review, which could prune low-growth/low-margin units (e.g., parts of Trust & Safety or Specialized Services) and redeploy capital

Large-scale transformation/outsourcing deal pipeline ('hundreds of millions of euros' of potential contracts under discussion, per FY2025 10-K-equivalent disclosure) as enterprises outsource more of the still ~68% of BPO-eligible work still performed in-house

AI partnership ecosystem (Microsoft Azure, ServiceNow, Kore.ai, Sanas, Parloa, Ema) positioning TP as an AI integrator/distributor for its large existing client base rather than purely a seat-based vendor
>EUR100 million in targeted annual run-rate cost savings from 90+ internal efficiency initiatives (AI-driven internal operations, SG&A reduction, organizational delayering)

business.risk: AI/automation disruption of the core labor-arbitrage business model
business.description: Generative and agentic AI (e.g., Klarna's public claims about AI handling customer service volumes in 2024) directly threaten the addressable market for human-staffed contact centers; TP's own data shows Trust & Safety revenue in sharp decline and 'continued acceleration of offshoring delivery' cannibalizing higher-cost seats. Management frames AI as a productivity tool it can monetize, but the market has repeatedly priced the stock as if AI is a net negative for volumes and pricing.

Despite diversification, large multinational clients can and do re-tender, in-source, or restructure contracts (e.g., non-renewal of a significant TLScontact visa-management contract dented Specialized Services revenue in H1 2026).

An expanding competitive set, from traditional BPO peers (Concentrix, TTEC, Foundever) to IT-services/consulting majors (Accenture, Cognizant, TCS, Capgemini) moving into digital business services, could force price concessions.

business.risk: Acquisition integration risk and goodwill impairment
business.description: Large, debt-funded acquisitions (notably Majorel, closed Nov 2023) carry integration risk and goodwill (~EUR 4.3bn at June 2026) that could require impairment if synergies or projected cash flows disappoint.

Founder-CEO Daniel Julien and long-serving deputy CEOs stepped down in March 2026, handing control to external hire Jorge Amar (ex-McKinsey); successful execution of Future Forward and the new strategic portfolio review is unproven.

financial.description: Net debt of EUR 4.0 billion at June 30, 2026 against EUR 4.2 billion of equity; TP issued EUR 1.2 billion of new bonds (4.75%/5.375% coupons) in May 2026 to refinance maturities, locking in materially higher interest costs than the bonds being replaced (0.25%/5.25%).

Revenue and costs are generated across EUR, USD, GBP, INR, PHP, COP, MXN, BRL, EGP and other currencies; euro strength versus USD/INR/GBP cut reported H1 2026 revenue by EUR 165 million versus constant currency.
Operations in hyperinflationary markets (e.g., Turkey, Argentina) create translation and purchasing-power volatility.
Refinancing in a higher-rate environment increases gross financing costs and could pressure free cash flow guidance if rates stay elevated.

regulatory.risk: Data privacy and cross-border data compliance (GDPR, CCPA, etc.)
regulatory.description: TP processes large volumes of sensitive client/consumer data across many jurisdictions; breach or non-compliance carries fines and reputational damage.

regulatory.risk: Labor and employment law / union relations
regulatory.description: History of labor disputes, including a 2023 'historic agreement' granting Colombian workers union rights after allegations of poor pay and conditions for content moderators; litigation and employee disputes remain a flagged risk category.

regulatory.risk: AI governance regulation (EU AI Act and similar)
regulatory.description: As TP embeds AI deeper into client operations, compliance obligations under the EU AI Act and similar frameworks increase; TP has sought ISO/IEC 42001 AI-management certification partly to pre-empt this.
TLScontact and similar public-sector-facing units depend on government outsourcing decisions and diplomatic/consular relationships that can change with little notice.

macro.description: TP's volumes are correlated with client-side consumer transaction and contact volumes; a broad consumer or corporate IT-spending slowdown would compress Core Services demand.

Higher-for-longer rates raise refinancing costs on TP's debt stack (evidenced by the May 2026 bond issue) and pressure equity valuation multiples for a company already trading at a depressed multiple.

Operations across ~100 countries, including Egypt, Tunisia, Turkey, Latin America and the Middle East, expose TP to political instability, sanctions regimes, and localized conflict risk (Russia/Ukraine exposure is immaterial at <0.3% of 2025 revenue, but broader MEA/Latin America risk is more material).

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The outsourced customer experience management market was an estimated USD 117-118 billion in 2025E (Everest), growing roughly 2% annually after a post-pandemic boom (2020-2022 CAGR of ~11%), reflecting both economic caution and the early-stage substitution effect of AI on contact volumes. The broader BPO/digital business services market TP is pivoting toward is roughly 4-6x larger (~USD 514bn in 2024, growing ~3.8%), with only ~32% of eligible work currently outsourced, leaving a long structural runway if TP can reposition from pure labor arbitrage to AI-enabled service delivery.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - revenue is contractual but transaction/volume-based components make it sensitive to client-side consumer and B2B activity; past downturns (e.g., COVID initial disruption, 2024-2026 AI-fear-driven slowdown) have shown real but manageable revenue elasticity, with resilience from multi-year contracts and diversified verticals.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - significant net debt (EUR 4.0bn) and recent refinancing at higher coupons (4.75%/5.375% vs 0.25%/5.25% replaced) directly raise interest expense; equity valuation (already depressed) is also sensitive to the discount rate applied to a lower-growth, higher-uncertainty cash flow stream.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High - revenue and costs span EUR, USD, GBP, INR, PHP, COP, MXN, BRL, EGP, MAD, TRY and more; the Group actively hedges via forward contracts and interest-rate hedges but reported results remain exposed to translation effects (EUR 165 million negative revenue impact in H1 2026 alone).
key_input_costs: Labor/personnel costs (the dominant cost line, ~70% of revenue)
Technology/cloud infrastructure and AI compute/licensing costs
Wage inflation in key delivery markets (notably Latin America, flagged explicitly in H1 2026 results)

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: revenue EUR 4,883m (-1.7% LFL, -4.5% reported), recurring EBITA margin stable at 13.6%, net profit EUR 216m (down from EUR 249m), net free cash flow EUR 243m; 2026 full-year guidance reaffirmed (0-2% LFL growth, ~14.6% EBITA margin, EUR 800-850m FCF).

Issued EUR 1.2 billion of new bonds (EUR 700m at 4.75% due 2032, EUR 500m at 5.375% due 2035) to refinance lower-coupon 2027/2028 maturities, extending average debt maturity but raising financing costs.

Governance overhaul: founder-CEO Daniel Julien and Deputy CEOs Thomas Mackenbrock and Olivier Rigaudy stepped down; Jorge Amar (former McKinsey Senior Partner/Global Lead of Digital Customer Care Practice) appointed CEO to accelerate the AI-driven transformation.

Q1 2026 like-for-like revenue down ~2.2%, below the full-year guidance range as expected ('soft start to the year'), driven by Trust & Safety decline and continued offshoring acceleration; management reaffirmed FY2026 targets.

Launch of 'Future Forward' strategic plan to reposition TP as an AI-augmented, next-generation digital business services company, including the TP.ai FAB (Foundational AI Backbone) AI orchestration platform and a formal strategic portfolio review (including potential divestitures/M&A).

Acquired 'Agents Only' (AI-augmented crowdsourcing platform) and announced AI partnerships with Sanas (real-time speech understanding), Parloa (agentic AI for CX) and Ema (horizontal agentic AI); also closed the ZP Better Together acquisition (language solutions for the deaf/hard-of-hearing community).

Sector-wide investor rotation out of BPO/call-center names on AI-disruption fears; short interest in TEP.PA reportedly rose above 12% of tradable shares by mid-2026 versus a ~2.4% peer average, and the stock traded near multi-year lows despite a single-digit forward P/E, reflecting persistent market skepticism about the durability of the labor-arbitrage model.

H1 2026 recurring EBITA margin was 13.6% (excluding restructuring/synergy costs), flat year-over-year; management expects efficiency savings to show more fully in H2 2026.

Core 2026-2028 mid-term objective under the Future Forward plan: return to 'sustained mid-single digit' LFL growth by 2028.

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Jorge Amar has framed 2026 as a transition year: 'a soft start to the year' in Q1/H1 with an expected H2 acceleration, driven by double-digit growth in AI-powered solutions and back-office/outcome-based activities offsetting a structural decline in Trust & Safety. Management explicitly does not expect any significant change in the Group's existing risk profile through H2 2026. The Board and CEO have also launched a formal strategic portfolio review, including potential divestitures and M&A, to concentrate capital on higher-growth, higher-margin lines of business, and continue to describe large (potentially 'hundreds of millions of euros') transformation deal discussions with existing clients as ongoing but uncertain in timing and outcome.

bull_case: Stock trades at a deeply depressed valuation (reportedly mid-single-digit forward P/E) reflecting worst-case AI-disruption fears that may be overstated given management's evidence of double-digit growth in AI-powered/back-office/data-services lines even as Trust & Safety shrinks

New, outside CEO (ex-McKinsey AI/CX expert) brings credibility to the 'AI-native' repositioning narrative and is driving a disciplined restructuring and portfolio-review program that could unlock margin expansion (targeting ~15.5% EBITA by 2028, up from ~14.6% in 2026) and meaningful free cash flow (~EUR 3bn cumulative 2026-2028)

#1 global scale, ~100-country delivery footprint, and 14-year average client tenure provide a durable platform to capture a greater share of the far larger (~USD 514bn) BPO/digital business services market, where only ~32% of eligible work is currently outsourced

Diversified client base (no client over 6% of revenue) and genuine AI partnership ecosystem (Microsoft, ServiceNow, Sanas, Parloa, Ema) position TP as a potential AI integrator for existing enterprise relationships rather than a pure casualty of automation

Shareholder returns have grown substantially even through the downturn (dividend per share up from EUR 2.40 to EUR 4.50, 2020-2025, with ~40% of net FCF returned via dividends/buybacks), suggesting management confidence in underlying cash generation
bear_case: Generative and agentic AI pose a genuine, structural threat to the core labor-arbitrage business model; Trust & Safety is already in sharp decline and 'continued acceleration of offshoring' signals clients substituting cheaper delivery (or automation) for TP's traditional higher-cost seats, with no guarantee the AI-powered growth lines will scale fast enough to offset legacy erosion

Elevated net debt (~EUR 4.0bn) refinanced in May 2026 at materially higher coupons (4.75%/5.375%) increases interest expense into an uncertain growth environment, while FY2026 guidance already implies only 0-2% like-for-like revenue growth

Leadership transition risk: founder and long-tenured deputy CEOs departed in March 2026, handing a complex, high-stakes AI transformation to an external hire with no prior P&L track record at TP; execution could disappoint as it has in prior guidance misses (e.g., 2024)

History of guidance misses and poor market communication (2024 stock collapse on a revenue miss, subsequent multi-year de-rating, high short interest reportedly above 12% of float in 2026) has damaged credibility, meaning even solid execution may take time to be rewarded by the market

Ongoing reputational and labor-practice risk (content moderation working conditions in Colombia and elsewhere, historical union-busting allegations, shareholder litigation) could resurface and pressure both ESG-sensitive investors and client retention
Currency headwinds (EUR strength against USD/INR/GBP) are a persistent drag on reported results and could worsen if the dollar continues to weaken against the euro
